figures.caption: Hands-on interactions with the Memetic Mixer

The Memetic Mixer, used as a design probe with four creative practitioners. To interact with the device, word tiles are placed on the dark rectangular region and the e-screen at the top displays words as they as placed (left) and the device’s response to them (right). techQuotes.text: The device uses physical word tiles, similar to those found in Magnetic Poetry [15], to provide input to the LLM.

The study evidences the specificity of individuals’ creative practice and the possibilities and tensions that arise when interacting with AI, contributing: • Qualitative accounts of in-depth experience of creative practitioners interactions with AI. • Examples of how language can be used as material interface for AI in creative practice.
Jacucci and Wagner [14] argue that material artefacts support collective creativity through their sensory and representational qualities, cautioning against a narrow focus on verbal expression alone.

Miguel Male, Spanish speaker Writer and Ethnographer Wary of AI tech I’m “a person who is sometimes very reluctant to incorporate … digital tools into the creative process.” “I have many more words in Spanish than I do in English” I frequently record notes and spontaneous thoughts in a hand written journal.
